decisions: I followed the contract where it differs from the design. replace fence on the limit path exits 1 and does not run stop.mjs itself; the coordinator then calls stop request/verify, and stop verify sets failed (§8.13/14; design R8 says replace runs stop).

acked_seq goes to run/acked.json and the alarm to run/alarm.json, not to coord.json (§8.4; design R6). status --endturn only checks the alarm. Each new watch --alarm kills the previous alarm (§8.5; design R6 says endturn re-arms it).
Events are `event` ledger lines; there is no events.jsonl (§8.3; layer L1). Intents are kept only for owner messages (R3), not for L1's five effects.
`--epoch` is always the row's current epoch. For stop on a fenced row, the attempt being stopped is epoch-1. On a committed row it is the current attempt (decision 17).

replace start, status and handover raise take the process list (PowerShell, which can be slow) before taking the run lock, then re-check the table and the ce inside the lock. This keeps the lock short so other scripts do not hit 75.

replace start does the whole build under the one lock: folder, manifest, row to admitted, admit line. If the folder already exists while the row is still at `stopped`, it is left over from a start that broke off, so it is removed and rebuilt. Any failure removes the partial folder and leaves the row at stopped.

The checkpoint is copied from every earlier attempt's cut prefix (each identical file once), not only from attempt e-1. Otherwise an attempt that was admitted but never ran would lose the prefix of the attempt before it.
Refusals with exit 1, 5 or 6 append an `incident` line (class refusal, R58). Exits 64, 65, 66, 67 and 75 write nothing, because a stale caller must not write.

B_tokens null (or gate:false) makes the budget check a reading, never a refusal (R45). The reservation is still computed and reported. A failed process list makes admission refuse with `slots-unknown`, so it fails safe.

admit check mode: with --task it exits 0 to admit, 6 when refused, and 2 when the facts cannot be read. Without --task it exits 0 if any candidate can start (or there are none), and 6 if every candidate is refused.

Watcher ticks: the first check a new watcher makes when it starts does not count as a tick, so hang is not counted on it. Each sleep of Δ adds one tick, and --once is exactly one tick. In the loop, main() reads the edge facts (now, free memory) once per tick.

Event dedupe: the watcher appends an event for (class, task, epoch) only when no unacknowledged line with the same key exists (seq > acked_seq). A condition that is already acknowledged does not cause another exit (but see the contract request on a `raised` field).
Hard and soft limits use floor(hard_frac*e_task) and floor(soft_frac*e_task) from thresholds, not the design's e - (Δ + latency) * peak rate, because no wall-clock rate may be derived.

Watcher intake is spawned only when no intake process is alive and some row is at started or bound. snap --new is skipped while f5_given is false. A step exiting 64 or 3 ends the intake. Any other non-zero step becomes an incident line and the intake continues. --no-intake is a test seam.
status --endturn writes acked.json first. It exits 2 when process liveness is unknown and 1 when either wake source is missing. It never starts or kills anything.

handover raise needs a `drain` line of its ce and quiescence (live+unknown+unconfirmed = 0 over every epoch). It kills the watcher and the alarm before raising, and still raises if a kill did not take, because the survivor exits 64 at its next check.
stop uses a session it finds only from a folder transcript (it names it in the ledger line), but never writes it to attempts[].session, which status --reconcile owns.

status `next` mapping: planned or stopped → replace-start (none while halted or draining); fenced → stop-session; stop-requested → stop-verify; admitted → start-session; started → bind; bound with a READY of the epoch → commit; failed, limit, or zombie spend over Z → owner.
contract_requests: [tasks-plan] format of plan/tasks-plan.json is not defined (§8.26 names the file only). replace plan needs per-entry {task, field, stage, role, steps, deps, question_ids, e_task}, possibly `tier`, and whether owner `approval` is required.

Who creates the first run/tasks.json: readTasks throws 67 on a missing file, and handover init is not a listed writer. Proposal: replace plan creates {schema_version:1, rev:0, tasks:[]} only when both tasks.json and tasks.json.prev are absent, so a deleted table is never silently recreated.

The variant V and the 'covered ids' (approved ids covered by a committed card, or a witnessed/confirmed card once F5 is given) are needed by replace (todo), stop (overflow ids), watch, status and admit (gate A). Cross-script imports are forbidden (§8.19), so please add lib.covered(root, row, {f5Given}) and lib.variant(root, row, ...). Please also define review-stage V concretely: which 'form slots' count (e.g. approaches without a verdict) and which cards are 'unchecked'.
[todo] format of wt/<task>-e<e>/view/todo.json is not defined. Suggested: {schema_version, task, epoch, todo: key[], covered: key[]}.

The layout of review-in/<task>/ is not defined. It needs the pack and its cards from the research dep's commit record (which step), the must-read snapshot texts, the protocol's fixed_files (relative to which base folder?), and the plants from sealed/plants/<task>/. Also: how the fresh reviewer's in/ copies it.

Rendering .claude/settings.json from a [profile] (permission rule syntax, the PreToolUse hook entry and its command line `node <root>/tcb/scripts/guard-hook.mjs --root --role --task --epoch`) must be fixed in the contract, because replace (U1a) writes it and guard-hook/audit (U3b/U4a) enforce the same file.

§2.1 lets replace write only in/, view/todo.json and .claude/settings.json in the attempt folder. A child needs .claude/agents/<type>.md copied from tcb/agents/ for its profile's agent_types (harness fact 3). Please add it to replace's paths.

Manifest [manifest] fields need sources. `tier`: profiles have no tier, so does it come from tasks-plan? `user_files`: which user-level files are hashed (a threshold list?). `outputs`: the step to kinds mapping. `schema_shas`: which schemas are listed.

Decision 17 needs stop request/verify on a committed row, but the §3.6 table allows stop only from active/fenced. Please add (committed, bound) → stop-requested → stopped with state kept committed. Please also confirm the --epoch meaning for stop: the row's epoch, with the target attempt = epoch-1 after a fence.

The [watcher] format needs a field to record conditions already raised and acknowledged, e.g. `raised: [{class, task?, epoch?, event_seq}]`. Without it, task-less classes (memory 24, common-cause 26, checker-batch 14, tamper 27) either re-wake the coordinator on every tick or can never be raised again once acknowledged.

Class 27 tamper-seen needs a machine-readable signal in the ledger. Which lines mean tamper: an fsck result value, an audit line with protected_writes, a check line with which reason codes? Proposal: every line written on an exit-3 path carries `data.exit: 3`.

Class 10 reopened: tms runs inside the detached intake, and its exit code 10 does not reach the watcher. Please define a ledger signal, e.g. a `check` line {check: 'dismissal-reopen', result: fail} written by tms, or a field in views/labels.json.

halted/draining are computed by admit, status and handover (drain check). Please add lib.runFlags(lines, ce) → {halted, draining} so the definition exists once: halted = a halt line not followed by owner act resume; draining = a drain line of the current ce.
An intent key pattern is not in §1.5 (status intent open --key). Suggested: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$.

R55 says admission compares gate.json's cut_sha and hazards_sha with 'the current cut and hazards object'. Please say where admit reads the current values: the last `cut` ledger line's sha, and which hazards object id?

Gate A before F5: with f5_given false no card can be witnessed, so gate A would block every review. Please confirm that a committed card counts as covering until F5 (as in R5) and that the unverifiable share is then only a reading.

A test seam is needed to make realProc fail inside a script that runs as a child process (stop verify not-run, status endturn exit 2). §6 forbids reading env vars other than PATH. Proposal: a threshold `proc_exe` passed to realProc({exe}) by scripts.

helpers.spawnSleeper() should take a marker (e.g. spawnSleeper({args:[marker]})) so its command line contains a folder path, `watch.mjs` or `--alarm`. lib.md T87 implies this, but the §4.11 signature does not show it.
No ledger kind records row creation by replace plan. Rows appear in tasks.json with no ledger trace. Optional: a `plan` kind {added[]}.
Watch takes its modes as flags (--once/--alarm/--intake), so §1.3 `mode` would be null. I specified mode null plus result.run; please confirm or make them positional modes.

Class 15 window-limit versus 16 drain needs a definition. I used: 16 when the coordinator's window ≥ W_star_coord (one drain line per ce); 15 when the coordinator's window ≥ W_quality, or a child's window ≥ W_star_child when that is a gate.
Please confirm the hard limit as floor(hard_frac*e_task). The design's formula is e - (Δ + wake latency) * peak rate.
§1.2 says main() reads the clock and free memory 'once'. A long-running watcher must read them on every tick, so please allow per-tick edge reads in watch.mjs's loop.
open_points: R48(a) says that in the pilot the watcher logs predicted against realised t_q per group. No ledger kind or input (predicted t_q per group) exists for it, so watch.mjs's spec leaves it out. A ruling is needed on whether it is a pilot item.
Checker-batch class 14: I read 'the only thing blocking a task' as 'cards await a checker and no row is at started or bound'. That is an approximation and needs confirming.
The precise review-stage V is unspecified (see the contract request). watch and status tests for review rows wait on it.
replace start for a fresh-review task depends on the review-in layout and on how plants (seed.mjs plant) are named. That fixture cannot be written until the contract fixes both.

Several needs-app items stay untestable: whether real session settings and agent files bind a session; whether claude.exe command lines name the folder or session id (attemptProcesses, taskkill /T); background-exit wakes, also across sleep and ce changes; and whether real transcripts match the parser (cwd, helpers, windows).

Other units' specs exist in spec/ (written in parallel). I did not read or change them. Cross-unit consistency, such as the commit intake/record flags I call from watch --intake, should be checked when the specs are merged.
